teamArchitecture.summary: The suite's team design is genuinely strong on verification discipline — context-isolated adversarial review, files-only role communication, capped loops with per-phase cap semantics, verify-or-revert, and an honest Orchestrator — but it is a QA-and-safety organization, not a complete engineering team. Nobody on the 18-role roster ever reviews code quality (the implement Code Reviewer explicitly disclaims it at grokbit-implement/references/roles.md:78), nobody owns durable tests for NEW behavior, nobody owns branch/PR/CI strategy (commits land directly on the checked-out branch), security review exists only after code is written, and there is no fast path — a typo fix draws the full ~25-invocation pipeline, which for the vibe-coder audience is exactly the retention failure the suite's own 3-question-cap rationale (grokbit-plan/references/loops.md:28) warns about but never applies to itself. The waterfall shape is better-mitigated than most (per-task verify commands, pre-implementation baseline, contract-defined backward edges), but three end-loading problems are unmitigated: security, visual feedback, and regression detection all arrive only at test time, and the test→implement hand-back can only append a task, so a design-shaped finding discovered at test has no route back to plan short of accumulating 3 unrelated deviations.
teamArchitecture.roster_assessment:
FULL ROSTER (18 named actors): Explore — Scope Setter (standard), Cartographer (cheap), Citation Checker (standard). Plan — Business Analyst (standard), Systems Analyst (cheap), Solutions Architect (expensive), Plan Reviewer (expensive). Implement — Build Engineer (cheap), Software Engineer (expensive), Supply Chain Security Analyst (cheap), Code Reviewer (expensive), Orchestrator (tier: none — the session itself). Test — QA Automation Engineer (expensive), Frontend QA Engineer (standard), Application Security Engineer (expensive), Release Engineer (standard), Maintenance Engineer (cheap). Document — Information Architect (standard), Documentation Engineer (cheap), Technical Writer (expensive), Docs QA (standard/expensive split by sub-duty).

REAL ROLES (distinct prompt + duty + context, and the distinctness is load-bearing): Systems Analyst / Solutions Architect / Plan Reviewer — the reviewer's isolation ("Not the architect's reasoning", grokbit-plan/references/roles.md:91; loops.md:69 "Context isolation is the whole mechanism") is world-class design. Software Engineer vs Code Reviewer — distinct duty, fresh-context mandate (grokbit-implement/references/loops.md:69). QA Automation vs AppSec vs Frontend QA — genuinely different disciplines with different tool grants. Docs QA fresh-reader — the strongest isolation in the suite (document only, no repo; grokbit-document/references/roles.md:74) and correctly declared unperformable without it (roles.md:86). The Orchestrator is honestly defined as not-a-role (grokbit-implement/references/roles.md:103-111) with a correct argument for why cross-session counting cannot be delegated — this is excellent, not ceremony. Tier economics are mostly rational and explicitly reasoned (e.g. grokbit-test/references/loops.md:146 warning against cheaping out on judgment-heavy verification).

CEREMONIAL/THIN: (1) Scope Setter (grokbit-explore/references/roles.md:7-13) — its entire duty is "restate the request, ask at most one question, do not explore." That is a prompt preamble wearing a role name; it has no distinct context (it receives the raw request, same as the session) and standard-tier cost for a two-line job. (2) Citation Checker is a strict subset of the Plan Reviewer's Grounding check (grokbit-explore/references/roles.md:27-33 vs grokbit-plan/references/roles.md:97) — defensible across phases, but it is the same duty under different rules (drop-or-flag, cap 2 vs severity-graded findings, cap 3).

OVERLOADED: QA Automation Engineer carries five distinct functions — baseline capture, regression replay, done-criteria coverage, failure triage (Loop T3), and baseline retirement (grokbit-test/references/roles.md:9-40) — plus the suite's most delicate write grants (two narrow test-file exceptions, roles.md:5). Triage in particular is debugging work, a different discipline stuffed into a QA role; in a world-class team root-cause analysis is its own function.

TIER TENSION: Release Engineer is standard-tier (grokbit-test/references/roles.md:96) yet renders the single most consequential judgment in the suite — SHIP / SHIP WITH CAVEATS / DO NOT SHIP folding in every other role's findings (roles.md:114-116). The mechanical part (any REGRESSION/CRITICAL → DO NOT SHIP) is fine at standard tier, but "SHIP WITH CAVEATS" and caveat operationalization is judgment work assigned below the tier the suite's own loops.md:146 says judgment requires.

SAME DUTY, TWO ROLES, DIFFERENT RULES: (a) Intake questioning — Scope Setter 1 question (explore/loops.md:16-18), Business Analyst 3 questions (plan/loops.md:22), Document gap-fill ask_cap 1-5 (document/SKILL.md:83); an Explore→Plan session can ask 4 questions across what the user experiences as one workflow, and the caps are never reconciled. (b) Secrets scanning — Code Reviewer checks "Secrets, keys, tokens" (implement/roles.md:95) with only IN_SCOPE/OUT_OF_SCOPE/INCIDENTAL disposal machinery; AppSec checks the same (test/roles.md:77) with CRITICAL-blocks-release machinery. A secret in an IN_SCOPE hunk fits none of the Code Reviewer's defined dispositions — the checks at implement/roles.md:89-95 have NO defined disposition path when they fire on an in-scope hunk (no severity, no block, no revert trigger). This is the roster's clearest unclear contract. (c) Debris — Code Reviewer flags debug residue/TODO per task pre-commit (implement/roles.md:94); Maintenance Engineer lists the same session-wide, advisory-only (test/roles.md:134-136). Partially defensible (dead-exports-across-tasks is genuinely invisible per-task) but the overlap is unacknowledged. (d) Dependency vetting — Supply Chain Analyst approves at install time (implement/roles.md:60-68); AppSec re-checks "dependencies added this session" at test time (test/roles.md:82) with no data flow between them: the AppSec engineer's inputs (roles.md:70) do not include the Analyst's verdicts.

THE STRUCTURAL HOLE: no role anywhere reviews the code itself. The Code Reviewer says so explicitly ("You are not reviewing code quality in general — you are answering one question: did this change do only what it claimed?", implement/roles.md:78). Test checks behavior, security, pixels, releasability, and debris. The only quality force is the Software Engineer's self-applied "match the conventions in 02-survey.md" (implement/roles.md:42) — an instruction with no reviewer. Design quality, clarity, duplication within new code, API shape, and the quality of any new tests are owned by nobody. A world-class team reviews every diff for these; this team never does.
